'''Gregor Luthe''' (born 19 October 1970) is a German [[chemist]], [[toxicologist]], [[nanotechnology|nanotechnologist]], [[inventor]] and [[entrepreneur]]. He is known for his work on toxicology of [[Polychlorinated biphenyl|PCBs]] and [[Polybrominated diphenyl ethers|PBDEs]].

==Early life==
Luthe was born in [[Epe, North Rhine-Westphalia|Epe]] on 19 October 1970, the only child of bricklayer and stove fitter Ewald Luthe and spinning mill worker Käthe Luthe, née Böcker.<ref name="wn_2016">{{cite web|url=http://www.wn.de/Muensterland/2016/09/2540772-Er-landete-als-Kind-auf-der-Sonderschule-Professor-Gregor-Luthe-Lieber-Gronau-als-Berkeley|title=Professor Gregor Luthe: Lieber Gronau als Berkeley / Gronau over Berkeley|author=Stefan Werding |editor=|publisher=Aschendorf Medien|work=Westfälische Nachrichten|date=20 September 2016 |access-date=2018-03-21 |language=German}}</ref> Luthe had a hard start at school as he stammered until 9th grade, when he learned to manage this, and leaped forward, leaving the lower education [[Hauptschule]] to enter the [[Gymnasium (Germany)|Gymnasium]] in [[Bad Bentheim|Bardel]], finishing it 1989 as best in class.<ref name="wn_2016" />

At the age of 19, he traveled to visit the [[German Democratic Republic]] two weeks before the [[Berlin Wall#The Fall|Fall of the Berlin Wall]]. Luthe was held for [[STASI]] questioning on 9 November 1989. He learned about this day's events only on the day of his release, the following morning.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scienceguide.nl/201410/alles-war-kopflos.aspx|title= Alles war kopflos (Everything was headless)|author=Gregor Luthe |date= 28 October 2014|editor=|publisher=ScienceGuide|access-date=23 August 2015 |language=German, Dutch}}</ref>

==Career==
Gregor Luthe studied chemistry, biology and physics at the [[University of Münster]] (1990 to 1995), where he specialized on fluorinated [[Structural analog|analogs]] of [[polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon]] compounds and graduated with the diploma.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/Chemie.ac/anders/groupalumni.html|title= Former Diploma and Master Students :: Current Group-Alumni |author= |editor=|publisher=Uni Münster, Research Group of Professor Dr. Jan Andersson |access-date=23 August 2015}}</ref> In 2002 he obtained his doctorate at the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]] (Netherlands). Starting 1996 he worked as a lecturer at the Saxion University of Applied Sciences in Enschede (Netherlands). As [[Marie Curie]] fellow of the European Council Luthe went to [[Trondheim]] (Norway) 2002 to 2005, where he was a senior researcher at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]], and also worked as the [[technical director]] and associate of the company ''Chiron''.<ref name="Marie Curie">{{cite web|url=http://www.appliedscience.nl/doc/121107_Presentatie_Gregor_Luthe.pdf|title= Introduction of Gregor Luthe (presentation) |author= |editor=|publisher=Saxion University of Applied Sciences |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031103042/http://www.appliedscience.nl/doc/121107_Presentatie_Gregor_Luthe.pdf| archive-date=31 October 2016}}</ref> 2005 he was awarded with the [[Feodor Lynen]] research scholarship of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]]<ref name="Humboldt">{{cite web|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/pub_hn_query.humboldtianer_details?p_externe_id=7000191938&p_lang=en|title= Humboldt Network, Query Details: Gregor Luthe |editor=|publisher=Alexander von Humboldt Foundation |access-date=17 August 2015 }}</ref> to study [[toxicology]] in [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]]<ref name="wn_2016" /><ref name="cv_saxion">{{cite web|url=http://www.saxion.nl/designentechnologie/site/over/lectoraten/nanotechnology/biographygregorluthe/|title=Biography Gregor Luthe |editor=|publisher=Saxion University of Applied Sciences |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140803084813/http://www.saxion.nl/designentechnologie/site/over/lectoraten/nanotechnology/biographygregorluthe/ |archive-date=3 August 2014 |access-date=15 November 2016 }}</ref><ref name="SIA">{{cite web|url=http://www.regieorgaan-sia.nl/binaries/content/documents/sia-nl/algemeen/documenten/thematische-impuls-htsm/thematische-impuls-htsm/subsites%3Adocument|title=Portret: Gregor Luthe en Paul Borm – Twee ondernemende nanotechnologen over het beter benutten van kennis en kunde / Portrait: Gregor Luthe and Paul Borm – Two Enterprising Nanotechnologists on the Better Use of Knowledge and Stichting Innovatie Alliantie|work=Thematische Impuls, HTSM |pages=30–35 |date=February 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180322081713/http://www.regieorgaan-sia.nl/binaries/content/documents/sia-nl/algemeen/documenten/thematische-impuls-htsm/thematische-impuls-htsm/subsites%3Adocument |archive-date=22 March 2018 |access-date=21 March 2018 |language=Dutch |format=pdf }}</ref> at the [[University of Iowa]] (USA), where he still is visiting professor and supervises doctorate students of the interdisciplinary graduate program in human toxicology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://toxicology.grad.uiowa.edu/faculty/gregor-luthe|title= Gregor Luthe |editor=|publisher=The University of Iowa|work=Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Human Toxicology |access-date=10 August 2015}}</ref> Luthe started investigating in e.g. the toxicology of [[Polychlorinated biphenyl|PCBs]] and [[Polybrominated diphenyl ethers|PBDEs]]. After some months as a lecturer at the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo]] he returned to Europe, to be a lecturer at the [[Saxion University of Applied Sciences]] in [[Enschede]] (Netherlands). 2007 to 2008 Luthe was additionally lecturer at the [[Jacobs University Bremen]]. In 2010 Gregor Luthe founded the company ''Windplussonne GmbH''.

In February 2012 Gregor Luthe was appointed Professor of Nanotechnology (''NanoBioInterface'') at Saxion in Enschede, which was the first Nanotechnology lectureship in the Netherlands.<ref name="cv_saxion"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scienceguide.nl/201202/eerste-nano-lectoraat-in-nederland.aspx |title= First Nano Chair of the Netherlands |editor=|publisher=ScienceGuide |date=10 February 2012 |access-date=10 October 2015 |language=Dutch }}</ref> The chair focuses on the development and application of NanoBio interface production techniques which are essential for medical, biological, toxicological and chemical applications, e.&nbsp;g. [[Lab-on-a-Chip]] devices. Luthe also engaged in multiple regional and international research partnerships and events, e.g. in January 2014 by establishing the ''Euregional Conference of Applied Nanotechnology'' (ECAN 2014) in Enschede, partnered by ''Alumni Nanotechnology Saxion'' (A.N.S), Saxion University of Applied Sciences, the MESA+ Institute for Nanotechnology ([[University of Twente]]) and [[CeNTech]] (University of Münster).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wn.de/Muensterland/Kreis-Borken/Gronau/2014/01/1417652-Konferenz-in-Enschede-Auf-dem-Weg-ins-Nanozeitalter |title= Conference in Enschede: Starting to the Nano Era |author= Martin Brock |editor=|publisher=Aschendorff Medien|work=Westfälische Nachrichten |date=15 January 2014 |access-date=20 October 2016 |language=German}}</ref> In September 2014 Gregor Luthe was co-initiating the cooperation of the University of Twente and Saxion University of Applied Sciences, to promote joint research in the field of Nanotechnology and to start the Netherlands' first Master's degree program in nanotechnology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.utwente.nl/ewi/ne/archive/!/2014/9/138200/saxion-and-university-of-twente-join-forces-in-nano-research |title= Saxion and University of Twente join forces in nano research |editor=|publisher=University of Twente |date=19 September 2014 |access-date=20 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031102920/https://www.utwente.nl/ewi/ne/archive/!/2014/9/138200/saxion-and-university-of-twente-join-forces-in-nano-research|archive-date=31 October 2016}}</ref> In 2014 Gregor Luthe founded the company ''Smart Material Printing'' with former students, to work on the production of new materials for 3D printing technologies as well as antibacterial surfaces. He also co-founded the company ''Nanobay – NB GmbH''. Gregor Luthe left his chair in Nanotechnology at Saxion in February 2015 to focus on his company activities.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.saxion.nl/desihnentechnologie/site/_news/vertrekgregorluthe/ |title=Vertrek lector Gregor Luthe |editor= |publisher=Saxion University of Applied Sciences |access-date=18 October 2016 |language=Dutch |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031102922/https://www.saxion.nl/desihnentechnologie/site/_news/vertrekgregorluthe/ |archive-date=31 October 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Luthe continues to engage in research projects and scientific work.

==Awards and memberships==
*2002: Marie Curie Scholarship of the European Council <ref name="Marie Curie"/>
*2005: Feodor Lynen Research Scholarship of the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation <ref name="Humboldt" /> 
*2007: Foreign Countries Tutor of the Germany Society of Chemists ([[Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker|GDCh]]) for the Netherlands<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gdch.de/netzwerk-strukturen/jungchemikerforum/auslandstutoren.html|title=DGCh > Structures > Young Chemists Forum > Foreign Countries Tutor in the Netherlands|language=German|editor=|publisher=Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker (DGCh) / German Chemical Society}}</ref>
*2013: Chosen among the 15 most inspiring professors of the Netherlands by ScienceGuide <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.saxion.nl/designentechnologie/site/_news/gregorluthe_obamasummit/|title= Gregor Luthe: Most inspiring lecturer of the Netherlands|editor=|publisher=Saxion University of Applied Sciences|date=5 March 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825192924/https://www.saxion.nl/designentechnologie/site/_news/gregorluthe_obamasummit/ |archive-date=25 August 2017 |access-date=15 November 2016 |language=Dutch}}</ref>
